questions.q: Propanoic acid is treated with SOCl₂ and the product is hydrogenated over Pd/BaSO₄. The final product is:
questions.explain: SOCl₂ gives CH₃CH₂COCl, and the Rosenmund reduction converts the acyl chloride into the aldehyde CH₃CH₂CHO with HCl as by-product.

questions.q: What is the role of BaSO₄ in the Rosenmund catalyst?
options: It lowers the activity of palladium so the aldehyde is not reduced to an alcohol
It is the actual hydrogenation catalyst
questions.explain: BaSO₄ has a low surface area and tempers palladium; an unpoisoned catalyst would reduce the aldehyde on to the primary alcohol.

questions.q: Which aldehyde CANNOT be prepared by the Rosenmund reduction?
questions.explain: Methanal would need formyl chloride, HCOCl, which is unstable at room temperature and decomposes to CO and HCl.

questions.q: If the Rosenmund catalyst is insufficiently poisoned, which side product is expected along with the primary alcohol?
questions.explain: Over-reduction gives the primary alcohol, which reacts with unreacted acyl chloride to form an ester.
